chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Aqabah, from Zakariya, from his father, from Yahya said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever cuts his nails on Thursday and leaves one to be cut on Friday, God will remove poverty from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of cutting nails on Thursday and leaving one for Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this practice of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), linking physical grooming on Thursday to spiritual and material well-being. The specific detail of leaving one nail for Friday reflects the Shia emphasis on preparing for the weekend of rest and prayer, while the promise of removing 'al-faqr' (poverty) underscores the holistic view of sustenance in Shia tradition. This act serves as a tangible means of grace (wasilah) connecting daily hygiene with divine provision.
